extracted.intended_audience: general readers and mathematicians interested in the history and practice of modern mathematics
extracted.subtask_description: Practices and standards for producing a comprehensive, axiomatic mathematical treatise and running a collective mathematical establishment (Bourbaki): choices of presentation, style, review process, organization, and community engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Axiomatic presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt an axiomatic presentation for the treatise, clearly formulating the basic rules (axioms) and deducing the related theorems by logical reasoning, expressed in simple terminology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The group’s goal was to give a 'backbone' to mathematics: start from clear axioms and deduce results logically. The first volume was devoted to set theory as the foundations. Aim for strict definitions of fundamentals and build necessary algebra, topology, and function theory from there.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hierarchy of abstract structures / unity of mathematics
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a hierarchical, abstract-structure organization that reflects mathematics' perceived unity (the treatise's title 'Éléments de Mathématique' emphasizing a single discipline).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure material so that foundational concepts support higher-level theories; present mathematics as a coherent whole rather than disparate subfields. The choice of the singular 'mathematic' signals this integrative ambition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear, simple terminology and consistent notation
rubrics_metrics.description: Use simple terminology and introduce consistent symbols and vocabulary (many terms and symbols introduced by Bourbaki became standard).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor precise, minimal wording and standardized notation (example: use of 'Ø' for the empty set). Consistency across volumes helps the treatise function as a unified reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strict, pared-down exposition (concise formal style)
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt a strict, pared-down style of writing: concise, formal exposition that emphasizes axioms and logical deductions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This austere style creates clarity and rigor but can be criticized as 'too dry' and lacking pedagogy; be aware of the trade-off between rigor/abstraction and accessibility. Complementary examples or diagrams may be necessary depending on audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include illustrative examples and diagrams (counterpoint to austerity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide examples and diagrams to clarify abstract exposition; omission of such material is a common criticism of overly formal treatises.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article notes Bourbaki was criticized for 'too few examples and diagrams' and for biases in certain presentations (e.g., measurement theory). Balance formalism with illustrative material when aiming for broader comprehension or pedagogical use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigorous collective review and iterative revision
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject each chapter to collective, detailed critique: chapters were read aloud, point by point, then revised by another member; repeat until agreement was reached.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use iterative, peer-driven processes for reliability and consensus. Expect intense debate and multiple revision cycles; designate drafters and require group approval before publication to maintain coherence and authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organize seminars selecting contemporary research topics
rubrics_metrics.description: Host seminars where invited speakers present on contemporary research topics chosen by the collective (the Bourbaki Seminar contributed to reputation and influence).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use seminars both to disseminate current research and to maintain the group's centrality in the mathematical community. Topic selection should be collective and aimed at reflecting contemporary advances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational secrecy and collective identity
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain a degree of secrecy and a shared pseudonymous identity for the collective; internal culture included self-mockery and rituals around the name and persona of 'Bourbaki'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secrecy shaped the group's public persona and internal governance; it can foster cohesion but also mystique. Be explicit about whether secrecy and anonymity are intended and how they affect authorship credit, recruitment, and public engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Membership renewal and retirement practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Institute rules for membership turnover (example: members must withdraw at the age of 50) to renew ranks over time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formalize membership terms to ensure generational renewal and continuity. Such rules influence institutional memory, stylistic continuity, and the balance between tradition and new perspectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long-term publication commitment and pacing
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain long-term, sustained publication efforts to build a monumental, structured treatise (Bourbaki achieved decades of continuous activity, though publication pace slowed over time).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan for multi-decade effort and realistic publication cadence; account for the increasing difficulty of covering a diversifying discipline. Diminishing output over time may reflect scope creep and field expansion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awareness of influence and potential pedagogical impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Be mindful of the treatise's broader influence (e.g., on curricula like the 'new math') and the risk of abstraction being inappropriate for certain educational levels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider downstream effects of formalism on education and practice; avoid assuming that axiomatic abstraction is suitable for all audiences or pedagogical reforms. Historical criticisms include perceived absurdity when applied to secondary education.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject-matter scope decisions (what to include/exclude)
rubrics_metrics.description: Deliberately choose subject coverage (criticism included absence of category theory and specific presentations like measurement theory), which affects the treatise's perceived completeness and biases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make explicit inclusion/exclusion criteria and be prepared to defend omissions; omissions can become focal points for criticism and shape the work's legacy.
